title: Juniper and the Inheritance
premise: When the diary of missing heiress Juniper Vale resurfaces in Sable Halloran's morgue—its entries continuing three weeks past her disappearance—Sable realizes the town's founding families have been laundering a century of secrets through a ledger disguised as the cemetery's burial records. As Sable decodes the ledger, she discovers Juniper is alive, hiding in plain sight as the estate's new housekeeper, and that the anniversary dinner is a trap set by the Vale patriarch to bury the last witness. At the dinner, Sable exposes the ledger before the town's elite, forcing Juniper out of hiding; the patriarch is arrested, but Sable must choose between publishing the truth that will destroy her neighbors' legacies or protecting the loyalty of the friend who helped hide Juniper.
about_author: Z. M. Quintana is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing county death records and swears half of them don't add up. They write mysteries from a converted funeral parlor office, where the filing cabinets still smell faintly of lilies.

chapters.title: Every Grave by Name
chapters.summary: Sable Halloran's POV. Establishing Sable's meticulous, solitary life as coroner in Hollow Creek, walking the cemetery she knows like a family album. A delivery arrives: a water-stained diary pulled from a flooded crypt, belonging to Juniper Vale, missing for one year. Emotional beat: quiet pride cracked by unease—the diary shouldn't exist.

chapters.title: The Date That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Reading the diary at night, Sable finds entries continuing nineteen days past Juniper's disappearance date, written in a hand that grows shakier. The final entry names the anniversary dinner. Emotional beat: professional skepticism curdling into dread as she verifies the handwriting against old medical files.

chapters.title: The Vale Anniversary
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable attends the town's gilded anniversary dinner under pretext of official business, observing patriarch Edmund Vale and his brittle family. She notices the new housekeeper flinch when Juniper's name is toasted. Emotional beat: alienation among wealth, first spark of recognition she can't place.

chapters.title: Ledger of Stone
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Comparing diary references to dates with the cemetery's burial register, Sable spots an impossible pattern: deaths recorded on days no bodies arrived. The gravestones themselves form columns of numbers. Emotional beat: the thrill of the hunt overtaking grief for a girl she once signed a death certificate for.

chapters.title: What the Ground Keeps
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: flashbacks from Juniper's diary interleave with Sable exhuming a permit-only plot to find it empty. The empty coffin matches a diary entry describing a midnight payment. Emotional beat: violation and resolve—someone powerful bought silence, and the ground was complicit.

chapters.title: The Housekeeper's Hands
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable interviews the housekeeper, Mara, noticing calluses inconsistent with service work and a scar matching one in Juniper's medical file. Mara deflects with practiced warmth. Emotional beat: suspicion warring with compassion—Mara's fear looks less like guilt than survival.

chapters.title: Old Money, Older Debts
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Digging into county archives, Sable learns the Vales' fortune traces to land seized during a flood that killed forty-one people—forty-one graves, forty-one ledger entries. Sheriff Dawes warns her off. Emotional beat: anger at realizing the whole town's prosperity is built on a buried crime.

chapters.title: A Friend in the Dark
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Diary flashback reveals Juniper discovered the ledger while cataloguing the estate and told only her childhood friend Ruthie—who urged her to run. Present-day Sable confronts Ruthie, now the town librarian, who denies everything too smoothly. Emotional beat: betrayal's first sting.

chapters.title: Nineteen Days
chapters.summary: Juniper's diary POV (interpolated chapters). Reconstructing Juniper's final known weeks: she copied the ledger, mailed fragments to herself, and staged her disappearance with Ruthie's help. Emotional beat: terror transforming into cunning—a girl deciding to become unfindable.

chapters.title: The Broken Cipher
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Working nights, Sable cracks the ledger's substitution scheme: gravestone birth-death years map to account numbers routed through a shell charity. Someone has been watching her car. Emotional beat: triumph shadowed by paranoia—the decoder has become the decoded.

chapters.title: Tail Lights on Chapel Road
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. After a near-accident staged on a fogged road, Sable suspects Edmund Vale but finds evidence pointing instead to his son Theo, who stands to lose everything if the truth surfaces. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into clarity about who benefits from her silence.

chapters.title: Ruthie's Confession
chapters.summary: Ruthie's POV. Cornered, Ruthie admits helping Juniper vanish but insists she doesn't know where she is—and reveals the diary was meant to reach Sable all along, because Sable once refused to falsify a report. Emotional beat: relief and guilt entwined; loyalty tested against truth.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sweeps the East Wing
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Following Mara after dark, Sable watches her leave a dead-drop of cash and food at the abandoned grange hall. Inside, signs of habitation: a woman living deliberately unseen. Emotional beat: heartbreak and certainty colliding—Juniper never left Hollow Creek at all.

chapters.title: Face to Face
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Sable meets Juniper in the grange hall. Juniper explains why she can't surface: Edmund controls the sheriff, the bank, and her grandmother's care. She asks Sable to wait until after the dinner, when the estate transfers to Theo. Emotional beat: fragile trust between two women who both refuse to lie.

chapters.title: The Grandmother's Room
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Visiting Edmund's bedridden mother under hospice pretense, Sable hears the matriarch murmur fragments confirming the flood-era crimes—and that Edmund killed once before to protect them. Emotional beat: horror softened by pity; corruption shown as inheritance passed down like china.

chapters.title: Theo's Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo privately offers Sable money and the original ledger pages if she lets Juniper stay gone until the transfer clears—he claims he's protecting Juniper from his father. Emotional beat: seduction of complicity; Sable recognizes how easily good intentions become accomplices.

chapters.title: Entries After the End
chapters.summary: Juniper's diary POV. Final interpolated chapter: Juniper reveals she kept writing past her 'death' deliberately, seeding the diary as a message only someone honest enough to check would find. Emotional beat: agency reclaimed—the missing girl authored her own rescue.

chapters.title: Sealed Indictments
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Sable compiles everything for the state attorney general, but learns Edmund has moved the dinner up two days and arranged for Juniper's grandmother to be relocated—smoke for a fire. Emotional beat: racing-clock urgency; the machinery of power moving faster than paper.

chapters.title: The Toast
chapters.summary: Multi-POV climax, part one. At the anniversary dinner, Edmund raises a glass to 'those we've lost.' Sable stands, produces the ledger, and reads the forty-one names aloud as staff freeze and guests' faces drain. Emotional beat: the room's glitter turning to ash in real time.

chapters.title: Juniper Rising
chapters.summary: Climax part two, Juniper's POV. Edmund attempts to have Sable removed; Juniper walks into the ballroom alive, holding the diary, and states her own name before the assembled town. Theo, cornered, turns over the original pages rather than inherit his father's crimes. Emotional beat: catharsis—the dead girl speaking.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Daylight
chapters.summary: Sable's POV. Edmund arrested; the state seizes the estate; Ruthie faces charges but cooperates. Sable must decide whether to publish the full ledger, knowing it will gut half the town's institutions—including the hospital that employs her friends. Emotional beat: the lonely weight of being the one who knows.

chapters.title: New Names on Old Stones
chapters.summary: Sable's POV, closing. Sable publishes everything, then walks the cemetery adding fresh flowers to the forty-one flood graves, finally named. Juniper, free, chooses to stay and rebuild. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace—truth cost the town its myths and gave two women back their lives.
